'''Emmanuel Grenier''' (born 3 November 1970) is a French mathematician. His research interests include [[hydrodynamics]] (e.g. [[Navier–Stokes equations]], [[Euler equations (fluid dynamics)|Euler equations]]) and [[mathematical and theoretical biology|mathematical biology]].

Grenier attended [[École Normale Supérieure]] from 1990 to 1994, before attaining his doctorate at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], under supervision of [[Yann Brenier]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=93285 }}</ref> He won an [[EMS Prize]] in 2000.<ref>[http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/ems_prize_winners.html History of prizes awarded at European Congresses of Mathematics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418072815/http://www.euro-math-soc.eu/ems_prize_winners.html |date=18 April 2012 }}, [[European Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2014-01-18.</ref>
